title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Reviews, Operational Tooling, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
summary: This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for defining and managing SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning guidance, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling recommendations, and a canonical runbook index. It consolidates operational expectations used by on-call, SREs, and service owners.
introduction: Purpose: Provide a single, practical reference for service owners and SREs to create measurable SLOs, operate error budgets, plan capacity, run reliability programs, conduct consistent incident reviews, and author/run runbooks. Scope: All customer-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deployments) and their supporting infra (API-gateway, inference-runtime, queueing, metrics/observability).
slo_overview: SLOs (Service Level Objectives) are the contract between service owners and SRE. Each SRE-managed service must define at least one availability SLO and one latency SLO where applicable. Guidance: - Measurables: uptime (success rate), p99 latency, provisioned throughput (reqs/sec), and embedding/indexing pipeline completion-time. - SLO format: available = successful_responses / total_requests over a rolling 30-day window. - Recommended targets: Hosted API availability: 99.95% (monthly), Dedicated control plane: 99.9% (monthly), Private deployment baseline: 99.5% (customer-specific). - Latency SLOs: p95 < 150ms for small text generation (short prompts) on hosted API; p99 < 600ms for tail-sensitive routes. Document the measurement queries and the exact TAGs/labels used in metrics (service, route, model, region, tier). - Measurement tooling: Use Prometheus for primary SLI calculation with recording rules; Grafana dashboards must expose SLO burn-down, rolling windows, and daily error rate table. - Ownership: service owner sets target; SRE validates, configures dashboards/alerts, and enforces error budget policy.
error_budget_policy: Error budget = (1 - SLO_target) * window. Policy summary: - Burn rate: Immediate pager if burn rate > 8x sustained for 1 hour. - Operational action: If burn rate > 2x for 24 hours schedule a mitigation plan and restrict risky releases until recovery. - Release gating: When error budget exhausted for a service for the current 28-day window, all non-critical releases are blocked until the budget recovers to > 50% of the expected remaining budget or a peer-reviewed mitigation plan is accepted. - Communication: Product and Eng leadership must be notified when a service drops below 30% remaining budget. - Calculation example: For 99.95% SLO over 28 days, allowed downtime = 0.05% * 28d = 0.0005 * 2,419,200s ≈ 1,210s. Error budget burn rate is measured against this allowance. - Monitoring: Grafana alerting for burn-rate, and a daily email summary table to service owners. - Exceptions: For planned maintenance windows, annotate SLO windows and subtract scheduled maintenance time from the SLI window (must be approved and recorded in the incident/maintenance calendar).
capacity_planning: Goals: keep 95th percentile latency within SLOs at target load with 20% headroom for traffic growth, 30% for peak events. Steps: 1) Baseline: collect 90/95/99 latency and CPU/GPU/KV-cache utilization over a three-week window; record request mix by route/model sequence length. 2) Demand modelling: project monthly growth using product metrics, conservation-of-workload assumptions, and planned feature rollouts. 3) Headroom policy: target 20% spare GPU capacity for normal operation, and ability to burst an additional 25% via autoscale/burst pools for flash events. 4) Capacity types: reserved (Dedicated), elastic (hosted autoscale), and private-provisioned (on-prem templates). 5) Run periodic load tests: quarterly synthetic tests and pre-launch smoke tests for any major model or kernel change. 6) Scaling knobs: batch size, concurrent streams, model quantization profile, and instance type. 7) Cost/latency trade-offs: document expected RPS and tokens/sec per instance type; include reference table (example in appendix). Responsibilities: SRE owns capacity forecasting and runbook creation; service owner provides growth forecasts and feature rollout windows.
reliability_initiatives: Programmatic approach: - Quarterly Reliability Sprints: focused initiatives (e.g., caching improvements, kernel optimization, autoscaler tuning) with measurable KPIs (reduce p99 by X, lower cost-per-token by Y). - Error budget driven work: prioritize reliability work when services approach budget exhaustion. - Chaos and game-days: run two game-days per quarter that test fallback behavior, model-fallback routing, and KV cache invalidation scenarios. - Post-deployment evaluation: every model or runtime change must pass a canary evaluation (traffic ramp, latency/cost/quality checks) and produce a rollback plan. - Reliability debt registry: maintain a tracked list of technical debt items with owners and estimated ROI. - Metrics for success: number of incidents impacting customer-facing SLOs, mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to repair (MTTR), and sustained error budget burn rate.
incident_review_standards: Purpose: ensure consistent, blameless, actionable post-incident reviews (PIRs). Standards: - Timeline: initial incident page within 30 minutes; priority notification to leadership within 60 minutes for Sev2+; postmortem draft within 72 hours; final review and action items closed or scheduled within 14 days. - Template fields: summary, timeline (UTC with event markers), detection method, root cause analysis (RCA), contributing factors, impact (customers affected, duration, SLO impact), mitigation/hotfix, long-term fixes (LTFs), owner(s), and status. - Root cause depth: prefer evidence-based RCA (logs, traces, config diffs) over speculative causes. - Severity definition: Severity aligned to SLO impact and customer impact (Sev1: SLO < 99% for > 30 minutes or widespread customer outage; Sev2: partial degradation or critical feature impacted; Sev3: minor degraded performance with workarounds). - Action items: each item must have an owner, due date, and acceptance criteria. Track in the reliability board and surface in QBRs. - Blameless culture: language guidance and reviewers checklist included in appendix. - Review cadence: PIRs for Sev1/2 require a mandatory review meeting within 7 business days with SRE, service owner, and product representative.
operational_tooling: Recommended stack and configuration guidance: - Metrics & Alerts: Prometheus (recording rules for SLIs) + Alertmanager (routing to on-call) + Grafana (SLO dashboards). - Tracing & Debugging: Tempo/OpenTelemetry for request tracing with service and route tags; sample trace retention: 30 days. - Logging: Loki + structured logs (JSON) with sampling for high-volume flows. - Incident Management: PagerDuty for on-call routing; incident pages in Confluence + Slack incident channel. - CI/CD and Canary: Argo Rollouts / Spinnaker for controlled rollouts with automated canary analysis tied to SLIs. - Capacity & Autoscaling: Karpenter/HPA for cloud; custom autoscaler for GPU-backed inference pools with linear ramp policies. - Chaos tooling: Litmus or Chaos Monkey for controlled fault injection. - Runbook tooling: Runbooks stored in Confluence, linked to Grafana alerts and PagerDuty runbook links. - Access & Audit: IAM roles mapped to on-call rotation; audit logs forwarded to centralized S3 and retention policy of 365 days for infra events. - Playbook snippets: include curl/CLI commands to repro common checks (latency SLI PromQL, burn-rate calculation, pod-level GPU util).
runbooks_index: This section lists canonical runbooks and how to use them. Each runbook entry below must include owner, pager escalation path, steps to mitigate, verification steps, and post-incident follow-up. Example entries: - API Gateway - high error rate: owner: api-platform-team; mitigation: rollback recent config, scale ingress, enable circuit breaker; verification: SLI p99 returns to baseline. - Inference Runtime - p99 latency spike: owner: serving-runtime; mitigation: enable fallback model routing, reduce batch sizes, drain and restart offending nodes; verification: tail latency stabilizes and error budget burn-rate decreases. - KV Cache - cache stampede: owner: infra-caching-team; mitigation: apply request coalescing, increase cache TTLs, warm hot-keys; verification: cache hit-rate restored > 95%. - Autoscaler - insufficient scale: owner: infra-autoscale; mitigation: increase scale limits, add temporary reserved capacity pool; verification: pods provisioned and SLOs meet targets. Runbook hygiene: review quarterly, test via runbook drills at least twice a year, and annotate each runbook with last-tested date and test-owner.
appendix_and_reference_tables: Appendix: sample PromQLs and example threshold tables. - SLI success rate PromQL (example): sum(rate(http_request_total{service="svc-name",status_code!~"5.."}[30d])) / sum(rate(http_request_total{service="svc-name"}[30d])) - Burn-rate PromQL (example): (1 - (sum(rate(http_request_total{service="svc-name",status_code!~"5.."}[1h])) / sum(rate(http_request_total{service="svc-name"}[1h])))) / (1 - 0.9995) - Capacity reference (example): g4dn.xlarge: 50 rps for short prompts, p95 latency 120ms; a2-highgpu-1g: 400 rps for embedding-only batch workloads, p95 90ms. - Contact list: on-call rotation owners, SRE leads, product liaisons, and incident commander pool. - Maintenance annotation process: document planned maintenance in the shared calendar, include affected SLO windows, and request SRE approval to exclude time from SLI windows.
next_steps_and_ownership: Action items: 1) All service owners must publish per-service SLO definitions in this directory within 30 days. 2) SRE will provision baseline SLO dashboards and alerting for the top 25 services within 60 days. 3) Schedule two runbook drills in the next quarter. Ownership: SRE (Ari Chen) for provisioning dashboards and runbook validation; Service Owners: finalize SLO targets and maintain runbooks. Contact: sre-oncall@redwood-inference.internal for urgent coordination.

notes_for_editors: Follow Confluence style: use headings, short intros, bulleted procedures, and tables. Avoid including sensitive customer data. For restricted/regulated services, set confidentiality to 'restricted' and list additional reviewers from security and legal.
